Definition: apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. slaver:--foaming.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in Luke's account of the boy with the spirit. The spirit takes him, he cries out, it tears him until he foams again, and bruising him, it hardly leaves him — the froth at the mouth is the visible mark of the torment.
TheologicalSignificance: A single ugly detail, and it does its work: the boy's suffering is real and bodily, not a figure of speech.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Demon-Possessed Boy
